title: Polynomials — Chapter Summary
intro: A polynomial is an algebraic expression with non-negative integer powers of the variable. The KEY ideas this chapter develops: zeros (roots) of a polynomial, the geometric meaning of zeros (x-axis crossings of the graph), the relations between zeros and coefficients (for quadratic and cubic polynomials), and the polynomial division algorithm.

sections.heading: Definition and Degree
bullets: Polynomial: aₙxⁿ + aₙ₋₁xⁿ⁻¹ + … + a₁x + a₀ with non-negative integer powers and aₙ ≠ 0.
Degree = highest power of x.
Degree 0 = constant; 1 = linear; 2 = quadratic; 3 = cubic; 4 = biquadratic.
x^(1/2), 1/x, etc. are NOT polynomial terms.
Value of p(x) at x = a is p(a) — substitute and simplify.

sections.heading: Zeros of a Polynomial
bullets: Zero (root) of p(x): a value x for which p(x) = 0.
A polynomial of degree n has AT MOST n real zeros.
Geometrically: real zeros = x-axis crossings of y = p(x).
Quadratic y = ax² + bx + c: parabola.
Discriminant D = b² − 4ac: D > 0 (two distinct real zeros), D = 0 (one repeated), D < 0 (none real).

sections.heading: Zeros and Coefficients — Quadratic
bullets: For ax² + bx + c with zeros α, β:
Sum: α + β = −b/a.
Product: αβ = c/a.
Build a quadratic with given zeros: p(x) = x² − (sum)x + (product).
Useful identities: α² + β² = (α+β)² − 2αβ; (α−β)² = (α+β)² − 4αβ.

sections.heading: Zeros and Coefficients — Cubic
bullets: For ax³ + bx² + cx + d with zeros α, β, γ:
Sum: α + β + γ = −b/a.
Sum of pair products: αβ + βγ + γα = c/a.
Product: αβγ = −d/a.
Pattern: alternating signs as the degree of the symmetric function increases.

sections.heading: Division Algorithm
bullets: Given p(x) and g(x) ≠ 0, there are unique q(x), r(x) with p(x) = g(x)·q(x) + r(x) and deg r < deg g (or r = 0).
Procedure: arrange in descending degree, divide leading terms, multiply, subtract, repeat.
Stop when the remainder has degree less than the divisor.
deg(quotient) = deg(p) − deg(g) (when r ≠ 0 you may sometimes have lower).
Useful for finding missing zeros: if α is a zero, divide by (x − α); the quotient gives the rest.

key_takeaways: Polynomial p(x) = aₙxⁿ + … + a₀ with non-negative integer powers.
Zero / root of p(x): value x with p(x) = 0; geometric = x-axis crossing.
Discriminant D = b² − 4ac decides nature of zeros for a quadratic.
For ax² + bx + c: α + β = −b/a; αβ = c/a.
For ax³ + bx² + cx + d: α + β + γ = −b/a; αβ+βγ+γα = c/a; αβγ = −d/a.
Build a quadratic from zeros: x² − (sum)x + (product).
Division algorithm: p = g·q + r with deg r < deg g; useful to find missing zeros.

glossary.definition: An expression aₙxⁿ + … + a₀ with non-negative integer powers and aₙ ≠ 0.
The highest power of x in a polynomial.
A value of x for which p(x) = 0.
A constant aᵢ multiplying x^i in a polynomial.
A polynomial of degree 1; ax + b.
A polynomial of degree 2; ax² + bx + c.
A polynomial of degree 3; ax³ + bx² + cx + d.
For a quadratic ax² + bx + c, the value b² − 4ac; determines the nature of the roots.
Identities expressing symmetric functions of the zeros in terms of the coefficients.
p(x) = g(x)·q(x) + r(x) with unique q, r and deg r < deg g (or r = 0).
The result of polynomial division; q(x) in p = g·q + r.
The leftover r(x) in polynomial division.
